config.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled

intro.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with two input fields to understand the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components in React. You will learn how controlled components manage form data via React state, while uncontrolled components rely on the DOM. The core concepts involve using React hooks like useState for state management and refs for direct DOM access. You'll implement both approaches in TypeScript to see how type safety enhances form handling. By the end, you'll know when to choose each pattern for your React applications.
intro.usecase: Understanding controlled vs uncontrolled components is essential when building interactive forms in applications like e-commerce checkout flows or user profile editors. In a controlled approach, React manages form state—ideal for real-time validation in sign-up forms where you need to disable the submit button until all fields are valid. Uncontrolled components are useful for file upload inputs where you only need the file on submission, or search filters that reset when a panel closes. This distinction helps developers choose the right pattern for scenarios like dashboards with live-updating charts (controlled) versus simple settings modals that discard changes on cancel (uncontrolled).

objectives: Implement controlled form inputs using React state and onChange handlers
Construct uncontrolled form inputs using refs to access DOM values
Configure form components to switch between controlled and uncontrolled patterns
Bind form data to React state for real-time validation and updates
Manipulate form submission behavior using both controlled and uncontrolled approaches
Initialize form values with default data in controlled components
Render dynamic form feedback based on controlled input values

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules for a project
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to React and the useState hook for managing state in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useState from the 'react' module.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a JSX element. For now, you can return a simple placeholder like a div or null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'App' and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a functional component named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize state for controlled input
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'controlledValue' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable for a text input
const [text, setText] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a state variable ready to store and update the value of a controlled input field.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into 'controlledValue' and 'setControlledValue' variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with an empty string and destructuring the array into 'controlledValue' and 'setControlledValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use the useState hook inside the App component to create a state variable named 'controlledValue' starting with an empty string value.

steps.title: Create change handler for controlled input
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named 'handleControlledChange' that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the 'controlledValue' state with the event's target value.
steps.hint: The function should use the setControlledValue state setter to update the state with the new value from the input event.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a properly typed change handler function that updates the controlledValue state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The handleControlledChange function is defined, takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes the correct event type parameter and updates the state with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The change handler isn't defined correctly. It should take a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and update the state with the event's target value.

steps.title: Add controlled input field with value and onChange
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add an input element with value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange}.
steps.hint: Use a standard input tag and bind its value and onChange attributes to the state and handler you created earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: controlled input binding
<input value={someState} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The return statement will contain an input element with value and onChange properly bound to the state and handler.
successCriteria: An input element is added with value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but it's missing either the value or onChange binding. Make sure both are present and correctly linked to controlledValue and handleControlledChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is not correctly added or the bindings are missing. Check that you're adding it inside the return statement with the proper attributes.

steps.title: Add uncontrolled input field with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a ref using useRef to store the uncontrolled input's value, and add an input element without a value prop.
steps.hint: Use useRef from React to create a ref object. Add an input element with a ref attribute pointing to your ref, but don't bind its value to state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ref for the uncontrolled input and an input element that uses it.
successCriteria: A ref is created with useRef and an input element with a ref attribute is added to the JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a ref using useRef and added an input element with a ref attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a ref and adding an uncontrolled input field. Try again.

steps.title: Create handler to read uncontrolled input value
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'getUncontrolledValue' inside your component that reads and returns the current value from the uncontrolled input's ref.
steps.hint: Create a function that accesses the ref's current property and returns its value. Remember to handle the case where the ref might not be initialized yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named getUncontrolledValue is defined that can read the current value from the uncontrolled input's ref.
successCriteria: The getUncontrolledValue function is defined inside the component and returns the ref's current value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named 'getUncontrolledValue' and returns the ref's current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't defined correctly. Try creating a function named 'getUncontrolledValue' that returns the ref's current value.

steps.title: Add button to read uncontrolled value
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the return statement that calls the 'getUncontrolledValue' function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with an onClick attribute that references your handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that triggers a function
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the function to read the uncontrolled input's value.
successCriteria: The button element is present with onClick={getUncontrolledValue}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure its onClick attribute is set to call getUncontrolledValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected to the getUncontrolledValue function.

steps.title: Add section headers and labels
steps.instruction: Add a heading element above the controlled input field to label it as 'Controlled Input' and another heading above the uncontrolled input field to label it as 'Uncontrolled Input'.
steps.hint: Use <h2> or <h3> elements with descriptive text to create clear sections in your UI.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding section headers

Controlled Input

Uncontrolled Input
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have clear section headers distinguishing between the controlled and uncontrolled input sections.
successCriteria: Two heading elements are added: one above the controlled input and one above the uncontrolled input with appropriate labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some headings, but make sure both sections have appropriate labels.
steps.feedbackWrong: The section headers are missing or incorrectly placed. Add headings above each input section.

steps.title: Style the component for clarity
steps.instruction: Add inline styles to the main div wrapper to create a clean layout with spacing and borders that visually separate the controlled and uncontrolled sections.
steps.hint: Use the style prop with an object containing CSS properties like padding, margin, border, and maxWidth to create a container with visual separation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main container div will have styling properties applied to create visual separation and improve layout clarity.
successCriteria: The main div wrapper has inline styles with at least padding and border properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but make sure to include padding and border properties on the main div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling wasn't applied correctly. Add inline styles to the main div wrapper with properties like padding and border.

steps.title: Test both input approaches
steps.instruction: Run the app in your development environment and interact with both input fields to observe the difference between controlled and uncontrolled behavior.
steps.hint: Start your development server if it's not already running, then open the app in your browser. Type in the controlled input and watch the display update immediately. Type in the uncontrolled input and click the button to see its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see two input sections with clear labels. The controlled input updates the displayed value immediately as you type. The uncontrolled input requires clicking the button to see its current value in an alert.
successCriteria: Controlled input updates display immediately on typing
Uncontrolled input value is read only when button is clicked
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress. Make sure both inputs are working: the controlled one should update the display as you type, and the uncontrolled one should show its value when you click the button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The app isn't working as expected. Check that your development server is running and that all the code is correctly implemented. Review the previous steps if needed.
